The Int↔Float conversions are recognized only at lower (→ f64.convert_i32_s /
i32.trunc_f64_s); inference had no scheme for them, so every use floored to
E_MissingVariable (175 in the wheel) and left a free var. A free var cannot
force the other operand of `float_of_int(n) * x` to Float, so x floored to i32
and the product emitted f64.mul on [f64, i32] — the standing m3 assembly error
in score_one_position.

float_to_int : Float -> Int, pure and monomorphic — so a call reads the type
live like any other, and the multiply unifies its operand to Float. The graph
now knows the primitive's type instead of re-deriving absence.

rungs 8/0, micros-through-m2 45/0 (no regression). First-light prerequisite:

sonido/8e710ad:
The one place that turns a canonical Patch into a live, compiled GraphEngine:
input/output + effect nodes + lazily-created split/merge junctions wired from
the patch's arbitrary edge list, then compiled, with per-node bypass and the A
snapshot applied (slot i == patch node i, so macro/morph targets address it
directly).

Effect construction is injected as a closure returning (effect, name), so the
firmware links only its curated PEDAL subset — keeping the 480 KB binary
small — while the plugin passes the full registry. The builder itself depends
on neither sonido-registry nor the effect set.

Host tests (registry as a dev-dependency; no cycle) build and *run* a linear
chain and a parallel split→[delay,reverb]→merge DAG, asserting finite output,
and check UnknownEffect / BadEndpoint reporting. Builds no_std for
thumbv7em-none-eabihf.

noodles/8edff54:
rerollSong has always scheduled a voice-pool trim after a roll, and it has
always been a no-op: trimVoices declines while playing, and the dice is
pressed while playing. So a layer pool's high-water mark was per SESSION
while any one song's working set is per SONG, and every reroll inherited
the peak of every song before it.

Measured on the built app, playing, rolling every 2.5 s and settling
(.tmp/dbg-roll-pool-ab.mjs): from a 346-source baseline, live audio sources
reached 641 after eight rolls and 670 after sixteen, and stayed — nearly
double, every one of them an oscillator or a forever-running param
ConstantSource the phone's audio thread pays for per sample. That is the
"fine on first load, worse after a few rolls" shape.

trimVoices grows an atBoundary form that runs while playing, keeping a
floor of 2 rather than 1 so the bar in progress doesn't rebuild from empty.
The refill objection the old comment raised doesn't apply at a roll: the
pool being trimmed belongs to a song that no longer exists. Safe
mid-playback by the invariant stealDontDrop already rests on — only
_availableVoices is touched, and the _makeVoiceAvailable guard refuses to
return a voice with anything on its timeline ahead of now, so the trim
cannot take one the lookAhead-early JIT has claimed.

rerollSong schedules two passes in BARS, not milliseconds: a reroll doesn't
stop the transport, so the old song's voices are never released — they fall
idle over the following bar, which is 1.5 s at 160 BPM and 4 s at 60.

Same burst now grows +149 instead of +324, and further boundary passes
reclaim nothing, so what remains is the current song's working set rather
than the session's residue. Sound-neutral; npm run smoke passes.
